item.description:
### Added - **Reply to herdr sessions from your phone.** Sessions running in herdr can now be answered and interrupted from the iPhone app, the same as tmux ones. - **Perch tells you when it can't reach your phone.** If notifications stop being delivered, Settings → Companion says so and shows the reason, instead of going quiet and looking like nothing was happening. - **A fleet window, and a keyboard shortcut that always works.** macOS hides menu bar icons when the bar gets full — and because Perch has no Dock icon, that could leave it running with nothing on screen to open it. Press **⌃⌥⌘P** to open your fleet in a real window you can resize, move and leave open beside your work. It's the same fleet you get from the menu bar, and it's also in ⚙︎ → Open Fleet Window. Turn the shortcut off in Settings → General if you'd rather have the key back.
### Fixed - **Usage bars could freeze at the wrong number.** A provider's usage percentage could stop updating and stay stale indefinitely — showing plenty of headroom on an account that had already hit its limit. Affected every provider's bars. - **Two agents in one folder can both be replied to.** Running two Claude sessions in the same project used to leave *both* of them without a reply box on the phone. - **A finished session stays finished.** A session that had ended could come back as idle and sit in the fleet indefinitely. - **Quiet days are visible in the Stats heatmap.** A day with a little activity was drawn so faintly it was almost identical to a day with none — measurably so, at a contrast ratio of 1.02 in the worst case, where 1.0 means "no difference at all". Active days now start darker, so you can see *that* you worked on a day, not only that you worked a lot. The Mac and iPhone grids had also drifted slightly apart; they now shade identically. - **The Stats filter says "All", not "Both".** It dated from when Perch tracked exactly two agents. There are six.
### Changed - **Settings is now four tabs** — General, Menu Bar, Notifications and Companion — instead of one long scrolling list. Pairing your iPhone, adding a licence key and picking a menu bar icon each have their own place, and Perch reopens on the tab you used last. - **Notifications stop piling up.** A session that finishes, then asks for approval, then finishes again used to leave a separate banner for each. Now the newest news about a session replaces the old, and everything about one project stacks together in Notification Center. Approval requests are still kept separate from each other, so a prompt can never be quietly buried by another one. - **Perch keeps still when you ask it to.** With Reduce Motion turned on in System Settings → Accessibility → Display, the menu bar icon stops animating, the thinking word stops rotating and the "needs you" dot stops pulsing. All three still show exactly what they showed before — they just hold still. - **Better with VoiceOver and larger text.** The menu bar now says what it means out loud ("Perch, 3 working, 1 waiting for you"), each session reads as one sentence instead of a dozen loose fragments, and the small text throughout the panel scales instead of staying fixed.
